definitions.explanation: An item that has been lost by its owner. A formal term used in official, legal, and transportation contexts such as train stations and police offices.

examples.japanese: {遺失物|いしつぶつ}の{届|とど}け{出|で}をした。
examples.english: I filed a lost property report.

examples.japanese: {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{取扱所|とりあつかいじょ}は{駅|えき}の{二階|にかい}にあります。
examples.english: The lost and found office is on the second floor of the station.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}に{届|とど}けられた{遺失物|いしつぶつ}は{三|さん}か{月|げつ}{保管|ほかん}される。
examples.english: Lost property turned in to the police is kept for three months.

notes:
USAGE:
This is the formal, official term seen on signs at train stations, airports, and police stations. In everyday conversation, {落|お}とし{物|もの} or {忘|わす}れ{物|もの} are more commonly used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{取扱所|とりあつかいじょ} (lost and found office)
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{届|とどけ} (lost property report)
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{法|ほう} (Lost Property Act)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {落|お}とし{物|もの}: something dropped; casual equivalent
- {忘|わす}れ{物|もの}: something left behind; more common in daily speech
